name: Riddles
desc: Riddles with a twist: Cairo street life, wordplay and puzzles that need a second think.

100: I talk in three colours, never out loud, and Cairo drivers argue with me all day. What am I?
A traffic light
I live in your pocket, I know all your secrets, and I panic when I reach 1%. What am I?
A phone
Men in shorts chase me for 90 minutes, and when they finally catch me, they kick me away. What am I?
A football
Every Eid I'm born in a cloud of flour and powdered sugar, and Grandma hides me in a tin. What am I?
Kahk
I'm a dessert named after a mother, not a chef. What am I?
Om Ali
I'm a football match with 22 players who never run, never sweat and are stuck on poles. What am I?
Table football (foosball)
I glow green in every cinema and only ever say one word: how to leave. What am I?
The EXIT sign
My face changes shape every night, and at the end of Sha'ban the whole country looks for me. What am I?
The Moon (the new crescent)
Two people hold one knife, everyone claps, and I lose a slice of myself. What am I?
A wedding cake
I bang a drum under your window at 3 a.m. in Ramadan, and nobody's angry with me. Who am I?
The mesaharati
Three people fight over me every night, and I always end up down the back of the sofa. What am I?
The TV remote
I'm a little kitchen on wheels that serves breakfast on the corner and is gone by noon. What am I?
The ful cart
I hang out of a microbus door shouting the stops and counting everyone's change. Who am I?
The tabbaa (the fare collector)
I come out of the oven puffed up like a balloon, and I'm on every Egyptian table. What am I?
Aish baladi (Egyptian bread)
I'm black and white, I stop when you wave, and my meter is somehow always 'broken'. What am I?
An old Cairo taxi
I sit on a plastic chair at the building's door and know everyone's business. Who am I?
The bawab
Fifteen pieces each, two dice and a lot of shouting at the ahwa. What game am I?
Tawla (backgammon)
I'm thrown over the bride's shoulder, and whoever catches me is 'next'. What am I?
The bouquet
You blow on me, make a wish, and I go out. What am I?
Birthday candles
I have three wheels and go down streets that buses are scared of. What am I?
A tuk-tuk
I'm red, they call me 'the club of the century', and half of Egypt loves my rival in white. Who am I?
Al Ahly
I was born in Nagrig, I cut in from the right wing, and Anfield calls me the Egyptian King. Who am I?
Mohamed Salah
200: I go off with a bang at sunset every day in Ramadan, and the whole city starts eating when I do. What am I?
The iftar cannon
I've been smiling in the same room in Paris for more than 200 years, behind bulletproof glass. Who am I?
The Mona Lisa
I'm the drums and dancing that walk the bride and groom into the hall. What am I?
The zaffa
A striker scores three times in a match, but his team doesn't get a single goal. How?
VAR ruled out all three
Two of me turn blue to prove you were ignored. What am I?
WhatsApp's read ticks
Egyptians promise everything will be done on me, and I never quite arrive. What day am I?
Bokra (tomorrow)
At the end of every exam I'm the only one allowed to make noise. What am I?
The bell
Ahmed has three daughters, and each daughter has one brother. How many children does Ahmed have?
Four
I'm the only fruit that wears its seeds on the outside. What am I?
A strawberry
Feed me coins and I give you a drink; kick me and I keep the coins. What am I?
A vending machine
I go up and down twelve floors all day without taking a step, and the bawab hates it when I break. What am I?
The lift
I'm the pharaohs' key of life, and people still wear me on a chain. What am I?
The ankh
I'm 'ahwa' in Cairo, 'qahwa' in the Gulf and 'kahve' in Istanbul. What am I?
Coffee
Every phone call in Egypt starts with me, and I mean the same in English. What word am I?
Alo (hello)
I flow the 'wrong' way, from south to north, and a whole country grew up on my banks. What am I?
The Nile
I'm famous for dying young, not for anything I did, and my tomb was found almost untouched. Who am I?
Tutankhamun
I have a lion's body and a king's face, and I lost my nose long before Napoleon arrived. What am I?
The Sphinx
Messi has eight of me, Ronaldo has five, and every striker dreams of one. What am I?
The Ballon d'Or
I'm drawn in brown on the bride's hands the night before her wedding. What am I?
Henna
Pots of me were found in the pharaohs' tombs, and I was still good to eat. What am I?
Honey
Pour hot water on me and I turn red; Egyptians drink me cold in summer and hot in winter. What am I?
Karkadeh (hibiscus)
300: Add one letter to the front of 'pain' and you get a country. Add one to the front of 'ran' and you get another. Which two?
Spain and Iran
I sat on the pharaoh's forehead, a snake ready to strike his enemies. What am I?
The uraeus (the royal cobra)
Which is the only country whose name in English starts with O?
Oman
My father is a donkey, my mother is a horse, and I can't have children of my own. What am I?
A mule
In football I send you off, in snooker I'm worth one point, and in Formula 1 I mean stop. What am I?
Red
In football I'm a warning, in the Tour de France I'm the leader's jersey, and in tennis I'm the ball. What am I?
Yellow
I'm a glass pyramid that guards a woman who smiles. What am I?
The Louvre Pyramid
I'm at the start of Aswan, the end of Giza and three times in Alexandria. What am I?
The letter A
A striker shoots, the keeper doesn't move, the ball hits the back of the net, and nobody celebrates. Why?
It was the warm-up
I'm an Arab country, my capital has my name, and I sit at the top of the Gulf. What am I?
Kuwait
The more cars drive over me, the bigger I get, and the government always says I'll be fixed next month. What am I?
A pothole
A camel has one or two, the Sphinx has none, and every Cairo street has hundreds. What are they?
Humps (speed bumps)
I'm a bridge, a city, a university and a national holiday, all with the same name. What am I?
6th of October
I'm a pharaoh, a railway station, a Cairo square and a famous hotel. What's my name?
Ramses
I'm a city, a canal and a crisis in 1956. What's my name?
Suez
Which African country hides inside the name of another African country?
Niger (inside Nigeria)
The more I'm forwarded, the faster I spread, and the less true I usually am. What am I?
A rumour (or a WhatsApp forward)
In a marathon, you overtake the runner in last place. What place are you in now?
Impossible: nobody is behind the last runner
Nine letters, a camera icon, and everyone's dinner gets photographed before it's eaten. What app am I?
Instagram
They call me the 'mother of the world', I have a thousand minarets, and my name means 'the victorious'. What am I?
Cairo
I'm a goddess with a cat's head, and the Egyptians made millions of mummies in my honour. Who am I?
Bastet
I'm on your wrist, I count your steps, and I buzz when your mum calls. What am I?
A smartwatch
400: In snooker I'm worth seven, in karate I'm the master's belt, and the All Blacks wear me. What am I?
Black
A man tells his doctor that every time he drinks tea, his eye hurts. What's the cure?
Take the spoon out of the glass
Name a country whose only vowel is A.
For example Canada, Panama, Madagascar or the Bahamas
I'm a city of the dead in Cairo, and people still live in me. What am I?
The City of the Dead (the Qarafa)
I was a pharaohs' capital, I'm a city in Tennessee where Elvis lived, and an NBA team carries my name. What am I?
Memphis
Which European country hides an Arab country inside its name?
Romania (Oman)
If a hen and a half lays an egg and a half in a day and a half, how many eggs does one hen lay in one day?
Two thirds of an egg
If 5 bakers bake 5 trays of bread in 5 minutes, how long do 100 bakers take to bake 100 trays?
5 minutes
Water hyacinth on a canal doubles every day and covers it completely on day 30. On which day was it half covered?
Day 29
Which is bigger: 2 to the power of 10, or 10 to the power of 3?
2 to the power of 10 (1,024 against 1,000)
If yesterday was Friday, what is the day after the day before yesterday?
Friday
I'm the only continent in all four hemispheres. Which am I?
Africa
Name a country whose capital has exactly the same name.
For example Kuwait, Djibouti, Singapore, Luxembourg, Monaco or the Vatican
I was Egypt's capital for nearly a thousand years; the sea swallowed my lighthouse and my library made me famous forever. What am I?
Alexandria
My builders changed my angle halfway up because I was going to collapse. What am I?
The Bent Pyramid
I was the tallest building on Earth for almost 4,000 years, until an English cathedral took my title. What am I?
The Great Pyramid
A train leaves Cairo for Alexandria at 60 km/h. An hour later another leaves Alexandria for Cairo at 80 km/h. When they meet, which one is closer to Cairo?
Neither: they're in the same place
Two boys are born to the same mother on the same day, in the same hour, but they aren't twins. How?
They're two of a set of triplets
What do you get if you add up every number from 1 to 100?
Which number, written in English, has as many letters as its own value?
Four
A man buys a camel for 60, sells it for 70, buys it back for 80 and sells it for 90. How much profit did he make?
In which Cairo market have gold, copper and spice sellers traded for more than 600 years?
Khan el-Khalili
500: Which letter doesn't appear in the name of any US state?
Q
Which number is exactly twice the sum of its digits?
A clock shows 3:15. What's the angle between the hour and minute hands?
7.5 degrees
How many times a day do a clock's hour and minute hands lie exactly on top of each other?
Which is the only capital city that borders two other countries?
Bratislava (Austria and Hungary)
Which English word means 'cheeky' and has all five vowels in order, a, e, i, o, u?
Facetious
What's the longest common English word you can type using only the top row of letters on a keyboard?
Typewriter
A keeper is so good that no ball gets past him all season, yet his team concedes 40 goals. How?
He's the sub keeper and never played
Which number, written in English, has its letters in reverse alphabetical order?
One
Which great African river crosses the equator twice?
The Congo
The Greeks heard the name of a Memphis temple, 'Hut-ka-Ptah', and turned it into the name of a whole country. Which?
Egypt
If you write every number from 1 to 100, how many times do you write the digit 9?
What's the smallest number you can divide by every number from 1 to 10 with nothing left over?
A snail climbs 3 m up a 10 m well every day and slides 2 m down every night. On which day does it get out?
Day 8
You have a 3-litre jug and a 5-litre jug and a tap. How do you measure exactly 4 litres?
Fill the 5, pour into the 3 (2 left), empty the 3, pour the 2 in, fill the 5 again and top up the 3: 4 left
How many people do you need in a room for it to be more likely than not that two share a birthday?
Which is the only country whose English name ends in H?
Bangladesh
Which six-letter English word, meaning 'nearly', has its letters in alphabetical order?
Almost
What comes next: 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, …?
33 (double it and take away 1)
Which planet is the only one whose English name isn't taken from a god?
Earth
